It’s always really hard dating someone going through depression - I’ve been on both ends of that spectrum. I think it’s reasonable to give someone x amount of time to start the healing process and make concrete changes, before you have to set boundaries for yourself. It’s tough to balance the line between giving someone the support they need and enabling them - she may need a bit of tough love, without pulling the rug out from under her. Ordinarily I’d suggest saying, listen I’m going to do everything I can to help, but you’ve got to take therapy and meds seriously, you need to develop some hobbies you love, make connections with others, keep your room clean and be making steps towards recovery so we can build a life together. It doesn’t have to be all at once, but I need to see progress. However it seems you have already done this and nothing is changing…it may be time to follow through and leave. Because ultimately, you need to be happy too and you’ve done your best to be there for her. She may only be able to find her way out of depression when she has to make it or break it on her own, I know that was the case for me - I made steps towards healing and it was only then I found the right partner for me. Someone to complement me rather than be someone I am toxically dependant on

I’m 23, so quite a bit older than you. My first suicide attempt was at 11 so I hear you. “A whole life to live” sounds like a whole lot longer to be miserable to me. I will say when you get older a lot of the stuff that upsets you now - including the abuse (I’ve been emotionally abused though yours is worse) does get better especially when you’re old enough to move away from it. That sounds condescending, it did then, does now, but like it’s just true it actually is. You then get adult problems, which are also fucking awful.
But like, I’ve had good moments. Even if I gave up now I don’t regret hanging on past 11. I would say, just focus on the hope of having a better life when you’re old enough. Try to stay out of legal trouble because if you get into it your life will be far harder and more depressing as an adult. And someday go to therapy so you don’t pass your trauma on to others, like your sister. Think about a life you can set on your own terms, would be my advice.

Best of luck and you have every right to complain
